alt.en: A plain printed title page in black-letter type inside a ruled frame: "National Hymn for the Colored People of America.", "Lift Every Voice and Sing.", "Words by J. W. Johnson. Music by Rosamond Johnson.", "(3)", "Published by Jos. W. Stern & Co., 34 East 21st Street, New York City." Top left, a Library of Congress stamp, "Two Copies Received Oct 19 1900", copyright entry "C-15499", "First Copy", with the number 63450 above it, and "Oct 19 1900" stamped again at the top; pencilled shelf marks at the foot.
alt.es: Una portada impresa sencilla, con letra gótica dentro de un marco de filetes: "National Hymn for the Colored People of America.", "Lift Every Voice and Sing.", "Words by J. W. Johnson. Music by Rosamond Johnson.", "(3)", "Published by Jos. W. Stern & Co., 34 East 21st Street, New York City." Arriba a la izquierda, un sello de la Biblioteca del Congreso, "Two Copies Received Oct 19 1900", registro de copyright "C-15499", "First Copy", con el número 63450 encima, y "Oct 19 1900" sellado otra vez arriba; signaturas a lápiz al pie.

caption.en: The title page of the 1900 sheet music, already called a "National Hymn for the Colored People of America": the song's earliest known printing, by Jos. W. Stern & Co. of New York, in the copy the Library of Congress stamped as received for copyright on 19 October 1900.
caption.es: La portada de la partitura de 1900, que ya la llamaba "National Hymn for the Colored People of America" (himno nacional para la gente de color de América): la primera impresión conocida de la canción, de Jos. W. Stern & Co. de Nueva York, en el ejemplar que la Biblioteca del Congreso selló como recibido para el registro de copyright el 19 de octubre de 1900.

source: J. W. Johnson (words) and Rosamond Johnson (music), "Lift Every Voice and Sing." National Hymn for the Colored People of America (New York: Jos. W. Stern & Co., 1900), plate 3071-3, title page; copyright deposit copy, C15499, received 19 October 1900
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1900 with notice (record: "©1900", "C15499 U.S. Copyright Office 19001019"); James Weldon Johnson died 1938, J. Rosamond Johnson 1954 (record: "1871-1938", "1873-1954"). US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: life plus 70 ended with 2024. The record's rights field is empty; faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).

alt.en: A page of printed music headed "Respectfully dedicated to Booker J. Washington", "Lift Every Voice and Sing.", "(National Hymn for The Colored People of America.)", "Words by J. W. Johnson", "Music by Rosamond Johnson", numbered 19, with an introduction marked "Allo. mod.e maestoso" in 6/8 on two staves marked "Simple way" over two marked "Piano or Organ", then voice and piano staves with three verses under the notes, from "Lift ev'ry voice and sing", "Stony the road we trod" and "God of our weary years", the note "If accompaniment is too difficult play voice parts", and the copyright lines at the foot.
alt.es: Una página de música impresa con el encabezado "Respectfully dedicated to Booker J. Washington", "Lift Every Voice and Sing.", "(National Hymn for The Colored People of America.)", "Words by J. W. Johnson", "Music by Rosamond Johnson", con el número 19, una introducción marcada "Allo. mod.e maestoso" en 6/8 en dos pentagramas marcados "Simple way" sobre otros dos marcados "Piano or Organ", luego pentagramas de voz y piano con tres estrofas bajo las notas, desde "Lift ev'ry voice and sing", "Stony the road we trod" y "God of our weary years", la nota "If accompaniment is too difficult play voice parts" y las líneas de copyright al pie.

caption.en: The first page of music in the 1900 printing, dedicated to Booker T. Washington, misprinted "Booker J. Washington": Rosamond Johnson's four voice parts, marked "Simple way", stand above a fuller part for "Piano or Organ", in A-flat and 6/8.
caption.es: La primera página de música de la impresión de 1900, dedicada a Booker T. Washington, con la errata "Booker J. Washington": las cuatro partes vocales de Rosamond Johnson, marcadas "Simple way" (forma sencilla), van sobre una parte más completa para "Piano or Organ" (piano u órgano), en La bemol y en 6/8.

source: J. W. Johnson (words) and Rosamond Johnson (music), "Lift Every Voice and Sing." National Hymn for the Colored People of America (New York: Jos. W. Stern & Co., 1900), plate 3071-3, first page of music (no. 19); copyright deposit copy, C15499
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1900 ("Copyright 1900 by Jos. W. Stern & Co." on the page); James Weldon Johnson died 1938, J. Rosamond Johnson 1954. US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: life plus 70 ended with 2024. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).

alt.en: Part of a page of printed music: a system marked "Grandioso", with the tune in octaves on a treble and a bass staff and three lines of words under it, "Sing a song full of the faith that the dark past has taught us", "We have come over a way that with tears has been watered", "Lest our feet stray from the places, our God, where we met Thee,", and below an organ part marked "Grandioso", "pp", "Sw. Bourdon.", "Sw.", "Gt.", then "ff" and "Gt. with Trumpets." over the last bar.
alt.es: Parte de una página de música impresa: un sistema marcado "Grandioso", con la melodía en octavas en un pentagrama de clave de sol y otro de clave de fa y tres líneas de letra debajo, "Sing a song full of the faith that the dark past has taught us", "We have come over a way that with tears has been watered", "Lest our feet stray from the places, our God, where we met Thee,", y debajo una parte de órgano marcada "Grandioso", "pp", "Sw. Bourdon.", "Sw.", "Gt.", y luego "ff" y "Gt. with Trumpets." sobre el último compás.

caption.en: At "Sing a song full of the faith" the 1900 printing turns "Grandioso": the voices sing the tune in octaves, while the organ starts very soft on the Swell's Bourdon and breaks out very loud, "Gt. with Trumpets", on "taught us".
caption.es: En "Sing a song full of the faith" la impresión de 1900 pasa a "Grandioso": las voces cantan la melodía en octavas, mientras el órgano empieza muy suave con el bordón del teclado expresivo y estalla muy fuerte, "Gt. with Trumpets" (gran órgano con trompetas), en "taught us".

source: J. W. Johnson (words) and Rosamond Johnson (music), "Lift Every Voice and Sing." National Hymn for the Colored People of America (New York: Jos. W. Stern & Co., 1900), plate 3071-3, second page of music, last system only; copyright deposit copy, C15499
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1900 (plate 3071-3, "Copyright 1900 by Jos. W. Stern & Co."); James Weldon Johnson died 1938, J. Rosamond Johnson 1954. US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: life plus 70 ended with 2024. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).

alt.en: A page of printed music numbered 3, headed "Lift Every Voice And Sing", "(National Negro Hymn)", "Mixed Quartette", "Words by James Weldon Johnson, Class '94", "Music by J. Rosamond Johnson", signed across the top right in ink "Very Sincerely J Rosamond Johnson", marked "Moderato e maestoso" in 6/8, with a piano introduction, staves for "Sop. and Altos" and "Tenors and Basses" with three verses under the notes, and copyright lines at the foot dated MCM, MCMXXVII and MCMXXVIII, plate 8088-3, "Made in U.S.A."
alt.es: Una página de música impresa con el número 3, con el encabezado "Lift Every Voice And Sing", "(National Negro Hymn)", "Mixed Quartette", "Words by James Weldon Johnson, Class '94", "Music by J. Rosamond Johnson", firmada en tinta arriba a la derecha "Very Sincerely J Rosamond Johnson", marcada "Moderato e maestoso" en 6/8, con una introducción de piano, pentagramas para "Sop. and Altos" y "Tenors and Basses" con tres estrofas bajo las notas, y al pie las líneas de copyright con fechas MCM, MCMXXVII y MCMXXVIII, plancha 8088-3, "Made in U.S.A."

caption.en: A later "Mixed Quartette" printing, subtitled "(National Negro Hymn)" and signed by J. Rosamond Johnson himself, now at Yale: the printing our parts were checked against.
caption.es: Una edición posterior para "Mixed Quartette" (cuarteto mixto), con el subtítulo "(National Negro Hymn)" (himno nacional negro) y firmada por el propio J. Rosamond Johnson, hoy en Yale: la edición con la que se comprobaron nuestras partes.

source: J. Rosamond Johnson, "Lift Every Voice and Sing" (National Negro Hymn), Mixed Quartette (New York: Edward B. Marks Music Co., 1928 or later), plate 8088-3, p. 3, signed by J. Rosamond Johnson; James Weldon Johnson Memorial Collection
library: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University
licenceEvidence: Every work on the page is by the two makers: the 1900 song and Rosamond Johnson's 1927 quartet setting ("Copyright MCMXXVII by Jas. W. Johnson and J. Rosamond Johnson", assigned to Marks 1928). US: published by 1928, so public domain since 1 January 2024 at the latest. EU and Israel: James Weldon Johnson died 1938, J. Rosamond Johnson 1954 (record), life plus 70 ended with 2024. Yale's rights field is a generic warning, not a claim (see rights.md).
